July 2013  
One of the most common types of advice we give at Y Combinator is
to do things that don't scale. A lot of would-be founders believe
that startups either take off or don't. You build something, make
it available, and if you've made a better mousetrap, people beat a
path to your door as promised. Or they don't, in which case the
market must not exist.
[[1](#f1n)]  
Actually startups take off because the founders make them take off.
There may be a handful that just grew by themselves, but usually
it takes some sort of push to get them going. A good metaphor would
be the cranks that car engines had before they got electric starters.
Once the engine was going, it would keep going, but there was a
separate and laborious process to get it going.

response:
# What Paul Graham Means by "Do Things That Don't Scale"

Based on the source corpus, Paul Graham's core concept is this: **startups don't succeed automatically—founders must actively push them forward through manual, labor-intensive efforts that won't scale.**

## The Key Insight

According to Graham's essay, many aspiring founders mistakenly believe that if they build a better product, customers will naturally come. In reality, startups require deliberate, hands-on work to gain initial traction. Graham uses a helpful metaphor: like the manual cranks used to start car engines before electric starters, there's a separate and laborious process needed to "get the engine going" before momentum takes over.

## Practical Application: Recruiting Users

The most common unscalable activity Graham identifies is **manually recruiting users**. Nearly all startups must do this in their early stages—personally reaching out to potential customers, understanding their needs, and persuading them to try your product. This work doesn't scale because it requires direct founder involvement, but it's essential to validate product-market fit.

## Resources for Deeper Understanding

For a comprehensive exploration of this concept, I recommend:

1. **[Do Things That Don't Scale](http://paulgraham.com/ds.html)** - Paul Graham's original essay (July 2013)
2. **[Dalton & Michael: What does it really mean to do things that don't scale?](https://www.ycombinator.com/library/If-dalton-michael-what-does-it-really-mean-to-do-things-that-don-t-scale)** - A practical breakdown by YC leaders Dalton Caldwell and Michael Seibel

The essence: **embrace the manual, unscalable work early on—it's how you build the momentum to eventually scale.**
